blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing FX at scale means moving from single trades to exposure aggregation. A large trade business receives dollars, euros, yen and rupees in hundreds of transactions a month, and pays out in another mix entirely. The task is not to hedge each trade but to understand the net exposure of the enterprise — and then decide what to do with it.

A mature FX programme has three layers. At the bottom, natural hedges — matching inflows and outflows in the same currency before doing anything else. In the middle, a rolling forward hedge programme that locks in a declining percentage of exposure over the next quarters. At the top, carefully judged tactical positions for unusual situations: a commodity move, a political event, a treasury officer with a view.

The discipline is not to predict currencies. It is to make sure that, however they move, the business remains close to its target margin. The CFOs who protect margin across cycles rarely make the most money in any single year — but they are still running the company five years later. That is the only test that matters.

items.q: According to the text, what is the central task when managing FX at scale?
options: To hedge every individual trade as it settles
To understand the net exposure of the enterprise
To predict the direction of each currency pair
To maximise profit in the strongest year
items.why: "The task is not to hedge each trade but to understand the net exposure of the enterprise."

items.q: Which layer sits at the bottom of a mature FX programme?
options: Tactical positions for unusual situations
A rolling forward hedge programme
Natural hedges matching inflows and outflows
Speculative currency bets
items.why: "At the bottom, natural hedges — matching inflows and outflows in the same currency."

items.q: What does the rolling forward programme do?
options: Locks in a declining percentage of exposure over coming quarters
Hedges the full exposure in a single contract
Reacts only to political events
Eliminates the need for natural hedges
items.why: "a rolling forward hedge programme that locks in a declining percentage of exposure over the next quarters."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Protecting the target margin matters more than any single year's profit
A treasurer who forecasts the euro correctly is running the programme well
Natural hedges should be exhausted before other layers are used
Longevity is the truest measure of an FX programme's success
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que a disciplina não é prever moedas — acertar o câmbio não é o sinal de um bom programa.

items.q: The final sentence, "That is the only test that matters," suggests that the author values…
options: the highest annual return above all else
survival and consistency across cycles over peak performance
the size of the tactical positions taken
the number of transactions processed each month
items.why: Inferência: os CFOs premiados são os que "ainda estão dirigindo a empresa cinco anos depois" — durabilidade, não o pico.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando o programa de FX ao comitê de tesouraria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm proposing today replaces the trade-by-trade approach we've been running, which, frankly, has been reactive at best. We hedge when someone remembers to, and we've been carrying exposures nobody had aggregated.

The new programme has three layers. First, natural hedges — before we buy a single forward, we match dollar inflows against dollar outflows, euros against euros. Last quarter, had we done that properly, we would have avoided roughly forty per cent of the contracts we actually placed. That's cost we simply didn't need to incur.

Second, a rolling forward programme that locks in a declining share of the net exposure over the coming quarters. And third — only third — tactical positions, reserved for genuinely unusual situations and signed off individually.

I want to be clear about what this is not. It is not a bet on where sterling or the real is heading. None of us can predict that reliably, and the programme doesn't ask us to. The single measure of success is whether we hold close to target margin, whatever the currencies do. Protect the margin across the cycle, and we'll still be here to run this desk in five years.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Harry describe the approach the new programme replaces?
options: Disciplined but too expensive
Reactive, hedging only when someone remembered to
Fully automated and rules-based
Focused entirely on tactical positions
items.why: "reactive at best. We hedge when someone remembers to."

items.q: What benefit does Harry attribute to natural hedges, using last quarter as an example?
options: They would have avoided roughly forty per cent of the contracts placed
They would have doubled the desk's trading profit
They would have removed the need for tactical positions
They would have predicted the euro's movement
items.why: "had we done that properly, we would have avoided roughly forty per cent of the contracts we actually placed."

items.q: How are tactical positions treated in Harry's programme?
options: They are the first layer applied
They are placed automatically each quarter
They are reserved for unusual situations and signed off individually
They replace the rolling forward programme
items.why: "tactical positions, reserved for genuinely unusual situations and signed off individually."

items.q: What can be inferred about Harry's view of currency forecasting?
options: He believes the desk can forecast sterling with enough data
He thinks reliable prediction is not realistic and the programme doesn't rely on it
He wants the committee to hire external forecasters
He sees forecasting as the programme's main strength
items.why: Inferência: "None of us can predict that reliably, and the programme doesn't ask us to."

items.q: What does Harry imply by "we'll still be here to run this desk in five years"?
options: The desk will grow its headcount over five years
Protecting margin is what lets the business survive over time
The programme guarantees the best return each year
Currency markets will stabilise within five years
items.why: Inferência: proteger a margem ao longo do ciclo é o que assegura a continuidade — não o lucro máximo de um ano.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Before hedging anything, we built a full picture through exposure aggregation." This means…
options: combining all currency exposures into a single enterprise-wide view
hedging each transaction the moment it settles
forecasting where each currency will trade next
cancelling contracts that overlap
items.why: Exposure aggregation = agregação de exposição: juntar tudo numa visão única da empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "By matching dollar receipts against dollar payments, the desk created a ___ before buying any forwards."
options: tactical position
natural hedge
target margin
rolling programme
items.why: Natural hedge = hedge natural: compensar entradas e saídas na mesma moeda sem instrumento.

items.q: Net exposure is best described as…
options: the total of all incoming transactions
what remains once inflows and outflows are offset against each other
the largest single trade of the month
the fee charged on a forward contract
items.why: Net exposure = exposição líquida: o saldo após compensar entradas e saídas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A ___ forward programme locks in a declining percentage of exposure quarter after quarter."
options: rolling
tactical
natural
reactive
items.why: Rolling hedge = hedge rolante: renovado e ajustado a cada período.

items.q: "The whole point is not to predict the currency, but to protect the target margin." Together these terms contrast…
options: forecasting the market versus defending the intended profit margin
buying forwards versus selling them
two different reporting currencies
short-term versus long-term contracts
items.why: To predict = prever; target margin = margem-alvo. A lição opõe prever o câmbio a proteger a margem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de tesouraria e hedge. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on each tactical position." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
quietly ignore
postpone indefinitely
publicly announce
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the three-layer programme desk by desk." To roll out means to…
options: implement in stages
shut down gradually
keep confidential
escalate to the board
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two treasurers pushed back on the tactical layer." They…
options: approved it at once
resisted or challenged it
rewrote the whole plan
delayed reading it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The desk approved the hedge policy but never followed through." They…
options: carried it out fully
failed to carry it to completion
handed it to another team
documented it in detail
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, o que faltou.

items.q: "Chasing the best year won't move the needle on long-term survival." This means it will…
options: make a decisive difference
not make a noticeable difference
raise costs sharply
take years to measure
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; com "won't", significa que não muda nada de fato.
